challenges.title: The 60-hour limit, reference period and POA

items.title: Absolute 60-hour weekly limit
items.text: S.I. No. 2/2005 sets an absolute maximum of 60 hours in any single calendar week for mobile road transport workers — on top of the 48-hour average limit.

items.title: 48-hour average over 4 months
items.text: The reference period for the 48-hour average limit is 4 months by default; an extension to 6 months is only possible through a collective or workforce agreement, not automatically as in other sectors.

items.title: Recording Period of Availability (POA) correctly
items.text: Waiting time at borders or during ferry crossings counts as POA rather than towards the 48-hour working time, but must still be recorded and made known to the worker in advance — a frequent source of error by hand.

solutions.title: How Klacks takes the load off logistics in Ireland
solutions.subtitle: From optimised routes to separately recorded POA — it all fits together.

items.title: Routes optimised automatically
items.text: Klacks sequences stops in the most sensible order — short journeys, time windows kept, fewer empty runs.

items.title: 60-hour and 48-hour limits monitored
items.text: Klacks checks the limits you have set up under S.I. No. 2/2005, both the absolute 60-hour weekly limit and the 48-hour average limit over the rolling 4-month reference period, live — correctly factoring in each driver's start date — and warns before a limit is exceeded. On request, Klacks blocks any breach in the automatic planning paths (e.g. wizard, suggestions, substitution); in manual planning, Klacks warns.

items.title: POA recorded separately
items.text: Klacks lets you record Periods of Availability (POA) as their own absence type not counted as working time, so they are visible in the roster and known to the worker in advance.

items.title: Matching licence categories
items.text: In automatic planning, Klacks only assigns routes to drivers with the matching licence — and warns before certificates expire. If a required document is missing or has expired, Klacks refuses the assignment, in manual planning too — only drivers with a valid licence are scheduled.

items.title: Installed on your premises: data stays in-house
items.text: Klacks runs on your own infrastructure — route and driver data stay in your organisation, and with a locally hosted AI model, for the AI too.

items.title: Klacksy understands your request
items.text: "Plan tomorrow's routes, driver Murphy is off sick" is enough — Klacksy starts the replanning, and the planning engine takes the configured working-time limits into account.
